A1.justification: Both readable 19-page PDFs describe the same OmniHuman dataset and OHBench study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and references support reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix, although both refer to supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original OHBench evaluations for I2AV and S2V in Tables 2–4, plus LTX-2 fine-tuning results in Section 5.3.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark evaluations in Tables 2–4 and the LTX-2 fine-tuning results in Section 5.3.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same filtering, subject tracking, pose estimation, audio-visual alignment, and hierarchical captioning pipeline. No algorithmic component or model procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same OmniHuman data and OHBench single-person, two-person, and person-object scenarios, with I2AV and S2V evaluations. No dataset, domain, or evaluated task changes.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain the same ten base I2AV models, and Table 4 retains the same six S2V methods, including MultiTalk and InfiniteTalk. Comparator membership is unchanged within each experiment.

E3.justification: The metrics, benchmark sample counts, approximately 5-second generation lengths, and resolutions closest to 720P remain unchanged. Section 5.3 retains 180,000 single-person and 20,000 two-person samples for LTX-2 fine-tuning.

E4.justification: The fine-tuning analysis in Section 5.3 and observations about shot scale and two-person identity errors in Section 5.2 are unchanged. No additional ablation, robustness test, or case study appears in the supplied v2 PDF.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates without repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4, the dataset statistics, performance plots, and qualitative findings retain the same results. For example, Table 2 reports LTX-2 and LTX-ft audio aesthetic scores of 3.69 and 4.13, respectively, in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions for tracking metadata, pose keypoints, synchronization intervals, and structured annotations in Section 3 are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: OmniHuman, automated hierarchical annotations, OHBench, and performance benefits from fine-tuning on 20% of the dataset.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 retains the same explanations involving training data and model architecture, and the same limitations involving interaction realism, distant shots, and two-person identity preservation.

D1.justification: The v2 abstract adds a code-availability statement and a GitHub repository link to julia-cherry/OmniHuman, absent from v1. Implementation settings and other reproducibility details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, comparisons with prior datasets and benchmarks, and all 62 reference entries are unchanged. Research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds one sentence about code access to the abstract and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining prose, section titles, and section order are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added abstract text causes layout shifts: Section 5.2 begins on page 12 instead of page 11, and Figure 6 moves down within page 14. All six figures and four tables retain their content, captions, and structure.

improvement.justification: The new code-availability statement and repository link provide a concrete implementation access point absent from v1, modestly improving reproducibility documentation. Scientific content and evidence are unchanged, and the layout shifts have little effect on readability. The PDFs alone do not establish whether the linked code is complete or runnable.
